Ben (Eng): Hey — I accepted a new role and my last day is next Friday. Quick Q about 401(k): can I roll over the balance after my termination date or do I need to do anything before I leave?
Samira (People Ops): Congrats! :tada: You can roll over after separation, but a couple of things to watch: outstanding loans, timing for required distributions, and whether the plan vendor needs a termination confirmation.
Ben (Eng): I do have an outstanding loan (around $6k). Does that block a rollover?
Samira (People Ops): If the loan isn't repaid, most plans treat the unpaid balance as a "deemed distribution" which can be taxable. Best to check vendor rules — some allow loan offsets into a cash distribution or you can repay within a short window.
Ben (Eng): Who do we use as the vendor? I can't remember the portal name.
Samira (People Ops): We're still on Guideline for the 401(k). Portal link: https://login.guideline.com/companies/redwood-inference (you'll need to sign in).
Ben (Eng): Cool. Any internal steps I need from People Ops to trigger paperwork?
Samira (People Ops): We'll confirm your termination with Guideline and provide the separation date. After that Guideline will email you options: rollover to IRA, rollover to new employer plan, or distribution.
Ben (Eng): If I roll to an IRA, is there any tax withholding to worry about?
Jules (Payroll): Quick note from payroll: direct trustee-to-trustee rollovers are typically non-taxable. If vendor issues a check to you personally, federal withholding may apply (mandatory 20%). So choose direct rollover to avoid withholding.
Ben (Eng): Good to know. About the outstanding loan: can I just pay it off through final payroll?
Jules (Payroll): If you want to repay via payroll deduction on your final paycheck, let us know ASAP — we have to set that up before final payroll runs. Otherwise the plan may auto-deem as distribution.
Ben (Eng): Final payroll is in 3 days, can someone confirm how to request the deduction?
Samira (People Ops): @Jules can set up a one-time deduction. Ben, DM Jules with the exact amount you want deducted. I'll flag this with Guideline too.
Jules (Payroll): I'll need: full name, employee ID, amount to deduct, and written consent (Slack DM is fine). I'll process today if Ben sends it now.
Ben (Eng): Sending DM now with details. Thanks all.
PlanBot: [system] Reminder: rollover forms may take 7-14 business days to process once vendor receives completed election.
Samira (People Ops): One more note — if you choose distribution and you're under 59½, expect potential 10% early withdrawal penalty plus income tax. Rollovers avoid that.
Ben (Eng): Got it. Appreciate the guidance.
Samira (People Ops): We'll follow up with confirmation once payroll and Guideline are updated. Ping here if anything changes. :+1:
